createoddsnends.jei.info.barrel_organ:
Plays book music. Right-click it with a book to load it, empty hand to take it back. Rotation into the back turns the pages, faster rotation plays faster.

The value box on its side switches between Play once and Loop. A redstone signal pauses it where it is. In Play once mode it gives a short redstone pulse when the song ends.

Wind lines carry the music out to wind chests, and every chest on the network gets every row.
createoddsnends.jei.info.wind_chest:
Blows the whistle on top of it whenever the organ plays a matching note. No boiler needed.

Put a dye in its filter to only listen to that voice. The value box on the back picks Exact pitch or Any octave.

Without a whistle it blows on any note it hears and gives off a redstone signal from its sides while it does, so it works as a sequencer.
createoddsnends.jei.info.wind_line: Thin copper pipe that joins the barrel organ to its wind chests. It connects on its own to other wind lines, chests and the organ.
createoddsnends.jei.info.card_punch:
Turns blank cards into punched card chains for the loom and book music for the organ. Right-click it to open the editor.

The Design tab is a pixel editor for tapestries up to 3 by 4 blocks. The Score tab is a piano roll with up to 1024 rows, and Import MIDI pulls notes in from a .mid file.

Save the design or score, put blank cards in and give it rotation. It takes cards as it goes, so long scores can be fed from a funnel.
createoddsnends.ponder.tag.cool_stuffs.d: The copy lathe, the jacquard loom, the barrel organ and the bits that go with them
createoddsnends.ponder.loom_build.text_1: The loom is three blocks wide, three tall and two deep, built from loom frames
createoddsnends.ponder.loom_build.text_2: The loom drive goes in the bottom front corner on the left
createoddsnends.ponder.loom_build.text_3: Leave the middle of the middle layer empty, the warp runs through there
createoddsnends.ponder.loom_build.text_4: The jacquard head goes on top, at the back in the middle. Its front is the loom's front
createoddsnends.ponder.loom_build.text_5: With a frame in the gap the wrench does nothing, and the message tells you which spot is wrong
createoddsnends.ponder.loom_build.text_6: Clear the gap and wrench the head again to put it together
createoddsnends.ponder.loom_build.text_7: Rotation goes into the side of the drive
createoddsnends.ponder.loom_build.text_8: Breaking any part takes the loom apart again
createoddsnends.ponder.loom_weaving.head: Weaving Tapestries
createoddsnends.ponder.loom_weaving.text: Right-click any part of the loom with a punched card chain to load it
Wool is its thread. Every wool block is 256 pixels of cloth, and it holds up to 64 of each colour
Give it rotation and it weaves the design, one throw of the shuttle for each colour in a row
If a colour runs out it stops with the shed open and carries on once you add more
The finished tapestry waits in the loom and the chain stays for the next one. An empty hand takes the tapestry, sneak to take the chain
Funnels, hoppers and mechanical arms work on any part: chains and wool go in, tapestries come out
createoddsnends.ponder.card_punch.text_1: Right-click the card punch to open its editor. Draw a design up to 3 blocks wide and 4 tall, then hit Save
createoddsnends.ponder.card_punch.text_2: Every block of height in the design takes 16 blank cards. Put them in its blank slot, or let a funnel feed them in
createoddsnends.ponder.card_punch.text_3: With rotation it punches the whole chain, card by card
createoddsnends.ponder.card_punch.text_4: The chain waits in the output slot until you take it out of the menu, or a funnel pulls it
createoddsnends.ponder.card_punch.text_5: To copy a chain or a tapestry, put it in the copy slot instead of saving a design. The copy keeps the same design
createoddsnends.ponder.loom_automation.t: A funnel on any part of the loom feeds wool straight into its thread
When a colour runs out the loom stops with the shed open. Goggles show which wool it wants
As soon as that colour arrives it picks up where it stopped
Funnels pull finished tapestries back out too, and the chain stays in for the next one
createoddsnends.ponder.tapestry.text_1: Right-click a wall with a tapestry to hang it, like a painting. It keeps the size of its design
createoddsnends.ponder.tapestry.text_2: On a floor it lies flat like a rug. The top of the design points the way you were facing
createoddsnends.ponder.tapestry.text_4: Hit it to take it down. The design stays on the item
createoddsnends.ponder.lathe_build.text_: A lathe sits on three lathe beds in a row
Headstock on one end, tailstock on the other. Place them looking along the bed so the headstock ends up on your left
The spot between them has to stay empty. If anything is off, the wrench fails and tells you where
With the middle clear, a wrench on any part puts it together
Rotation goes into the back of the headstock
Breaking any part takes the whole lathe apart again
createoddsnends.ponder.lathe_cutting.tex: Right-click the lathe with a written profile template
Then with the block you want turned. Most full blocks work
Give it rotation and the cutter works along the piece, following the template
Take the finished piece out with an empty hand. Sneak to take the template back
Funnels, hoppers and mechanical arms can feed blocks in and pull pieces out from any lathe part
createoddsnends.ponder.lathe_tracer.head: Copying a Master with the Tracer
createoddsnends.ponder.lathe_tracer.text: A tracer row goes two blocks behind the lathe: three rails, a holder over each end, the middle left empty
Wrench the lathe again and the tracer joins it
Right-click a holder with any turned piece to load it as the master. It wins over the template
The stylus rides the master and the cutter copies it, no template needed
Pull the master out mid cut and the lathe just waits, keeping its progress until a master or template is back
Funnels on the tracer row load masters too
createoddsnends.ponder.template_table.te: The template table writes shapes onto profile templates. Put a template in the slot
Each of the 16 bars is one layer, foot at the left. Drag them to set how wide the piece is there, then hit Save
Or sneak-click a turned piece with a template to copy its shape
createoddsnends.ponder.organ_basics.head: Playing Book Music
createoddsnends.ponder.organ_basics.text: The barrel organ is two blocks tall. Its front faces you when you place it
Rotation goes into the back. Faster rotation plays faster
Right-click it with book music from the card punch to load it. An empty hand takes it back out
It plays the book from the start, turning the pages as it goes
On Play once it stops at the end and sends out a short redstone pulse
The value box on its side switches it to Loop, and it starts over every time it reaches the end
A redstone signal on either half pauses it. Turn it off and it carries on from the same spot
createoddsnends.ponder.wind_network.head: Wind Chests and Whistles
createoddsnends.ponder.wind_network.text: Wind lines carry the music from the organ. They join up with each other on their own
Wind chests go anywhere on the lines. Every chest on the network hears every note
Put a steam whistle on a chest. It blows whenever the organ plays that whistle's note, no boiler needed
Whistle size and extensions set the pitch, the same way they always do
Put a dye in the filter on the front to make a chest listen to one voice of the score only
The value box on the back picks Exact pitch, or Any octave so one whistle covers that note all the way up and down
createoddsnends.ponder.wind_sequencer.te: A wind chest with no whistle on top still blows on any note it hears, as long as it matches the filter
While it blows it gives off a redstone signal from its sides, so it can drive lamps, doors or anything else
Give each chest a different voice and the score plays your redstone like a sequencer
